claims.text: Integrating machine-learning potentials into computational workflows can be used to assess phase stability in crystalline materials.
Integrating machine-learning potentials into computational workflows can be used for microstructure refinement in crystalline materials.
Integrating machine-learning potentials into computational workflows can be used for property optimization in crystalline materials.
The proposed workflow integrates machine-learning potentials with ab initio calculations.
Machine-learning potentials predict phase stability through ab initio calculations and machine-learning algorithms.
Machine-learning potentials enable microstructure refinement through ab initio calculations and machine-learning algorithms.
Machine-learning potentials enable property optimization through ab initio calculations and machine-learning algorithms.
The workflow will improve phase stability by 15% relative to trial-and-error approaches.
The workflow will improve microstructure refinement by 20% relative to trial-and-error approaches.
The workflow will improve property optimization by 12% relative to trial-and-error approaches.
The proposed method is applicable from -200°C to 1000°C.
The proposed method is applicable from 1 atm to 1000 atm.
The accuracy of machine-learning potentials may be uncertain for complex crystalline materials.
Computational resources and data quality may limit the proposed workflow.
The hypothesis is falsified if improvements in all three target measures are less than 5% relative to baseline.
